static_scope.collision: Shared exact static concave hull/deck solids; no playable deck claim.

game_source.authored_deck_clearance: Aft deck break ends at-.35L, clear of actual mizzen chainplate at-.3364L and first gun at-.31L. No fastening is embedded in the transverse bulkhead.

cabin.berth_omission_reason: The narrow pointed after cuddy cannot support a freestanding adult berth and a clear aisle on the authored sole. A modest hinged seat locker combining seating and storage are inferred; no grand cabin or recovered historical bed arrangement is claimed.

detailed_layout.confidence: Authored reconstruction informed by read source material, not a recovered stock game interior.
notes: Shallow framed hold -0.30L to +0.38L, sole -0.85 m; an actual fitted water cask and planked provisions box occupy supported side footprints. The narrow forward area stays clear; no invisible cable locker is claimed.
Low after cabin -0.47L to -0.35L, floor -0.25 m and modest hinged seat locker combining seating and storage, with no unsupported freestanding adult berth; no stacked gun decks.
2.0 × 1.4 m centerline hatch at +0.13L, offset poop companion, visible pump and belaying fittings.
Twenty open-deck guns retain clear working lanes; three lateen yards, detailed lead blocks and restrained stern rail/trim distinguish the fitting-out.
Le Requin is a family analogue, not a reproduction or a stock game interior plan.
Oars are a historical xebec trait but the reconstruction does not invent a full rowing battery or change the POTC armament.
One offset descending companion enters the cabin through its forward door. No redundant hole is cut through the short cabin roof; this preserves useful furniture and working-deck area.
detailed_layout.dimension_status: Dimensions, frame spacing, compartments and fitting positions are authored estimates fitted to the preserved POTC-family hull. These sources do not document the proprietary retail model and do not establish exact stock interiors. No museum image is copied into the model or its textures.
